Hook answer surface: PreToolUse hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision allow|deny|ask|defer; PermissionRequest hookSpecificOutput.decision.behavior allow|deny (+updatedInput); Stop top-level decision "block" + reason. Exit 2 blocks on PreToolUse and is ignored by PermissionRequest; other exit codes are non-blocking.

Hook transport: type "http" POSTs the event's stdin JSON to a url. Non-2xx or connection failure is a non-blocking error, so the terminal prompt falls through. Blocking requires a 2xx JSON decision or onFailure "block" (v2.1.295+). Default timeout 600s. Command hooks also support async.

architect.rationale: MECHANISM: the MVP answers only sessions Orchestra spawns itself, as headless claude -p --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json --verbose --include-hook-events children driven from Rust over stdin/stdout. It is the only path that covers all three answer kinds in the goal (tool permission, AskUserQuestion, free-text reply after a turn ends) without editing the user settings and without bundling a Node runtime. Permission and AskUserQuestion prompts are expected as stream-json control requests when --permission-prompt-tool stdio is passed (the channel the Agent SDK canUseTool rides on); a free-text reply is the next stream-json user message after a result. Those names, the flag and multi-turn stdin are UNVERIFIED, so s1 is a spike that resolves them and commits redacted fixtures, and s2 is built and tested against those fixtures. The --settings hook-merge unknown is designed around, not spiked: the MVP passes no --settings and installs no hooks. Status comes from the stream itself (system init, assistant, control_request, result, process exit); hook events surfaced by --include-hook-events are consumed when present, but nothing depends on them. GOAL READING: tracks sessions via their hooks reads two ways: (A) observe any terminal claude the user launches through hooks written into user settings; (B) track the sessions the app launches through their own event stream. A cannot answer AskUserQuestion or free text (scout plan-killer) and needs a user-config edit; B satisfies answer-on-desktop fully. Recommend B; A is in not_doing as a follow-on run. SHAPE: diamond. Three slices with disjoint file sets, each with a standalone done_when, and this is the first real code in the app (process spawning plus IPC), which should not merge unreviewed. Disjoint sets: s1 = src-tauri/tests/fixtures/stream_json/** only (data + README, no code); s2 = src-tauri/src/**, src-tauri/Cargo.toml, src-tauri/Cargo.lock (currently untracked); s2 is the ONLY slice touching lib.rs and Cargo.toml, so there is no shared-file sequencing; s3 = desktop/src/**, desktop/index.html, desktop/package.json, desktop/package-lock.json. No slice touches tauri.conf.json or capabilities/: app commands and events are covered by core:default, and the dialog plugin is called from Rust only, so no JS permission is needed; a builder that finds otherwise stops and asks for a scope exception. s3 runs in parallel because it consumes only the IPC contract pinned verbatim in ipc_contract, not anything s1 or s2 produce. RISK: s1 high because it captures real session transcripts carrying the owner username, home path, cwd, session ids and possibly account metadata, and a grep cannot prove redaction. s2 high because it spawns child processes and exposes IPC: no-frontend-string-as-path-or-command, no shell, CREATE_NO_WINDOW, child cleanup on exit and path-free error strings are rules no unit test fully sees; it also adds a crate. s3 low because it has no sensitive data, shares no file with another slice, touches no tauri.conf/capabilities, and the contract it must match is pinned as text here so the scope check is a direct comparison; tsc plus vitest cover the logic it owns. POST-SPIKE GATE: if s1 records VERDICT: FALSIFIED, s2 does not start and the run returns to architect. The fallback is a PermissionRequest http hook injected per spawn via --settings to a loopback listener, which needs its own spike of the --settings merge unknown.

commands.pick_project: () -> Option<Project>. Rust opens the native folder picker itself (tauri-plugin-dialog, Rust API only); the absolute path stays in Rust state; the frontend only ever sees Project{id,name} where name is the folder basename.
commands.start_session: (args: {project_id: string, prompt: string}) -> SessionSummary. project_id must exist; prompt non-empty and <= 32768 bytes; prompt is written to the child stdin as a stream-json user message, never passed as a CLI argument.
commands.answer: (args: Answer) -> void. Answer is a serde-tagged enum on kind: {kind:permission, item_id:string, decision:allow|deny, message?:string} | {kind:question, item_id:string, answers: Record<string,string>} | {kind:reply, session_id:string, text:string}. Unknown/resolved item_id, unknown session_id, empty or >32768-byte text -> Err(string) with no path in it.
commands.stop_session: (args: {session_id: string}) -> void. Kills the child process.

types.SessionStatus: starting | working | waiting_permission | waiting_question | idle | ended | failed
types.SessionSummary: {id: string, project_id: string, project_name: string, status: SessionStatus, started_at: number (ms epoch), last_activity_at: number, last_message: string|null (truncated to 500 chars), claude_session_id: string|null}
types.InboxItem: {id: string, session_id: string, kind: permission|question|finished|error, created_at: number, resolved: boolean, summary: string (truncated), tool_name: string|null, tool_input_preview: string|null (JSON, truncated to 2000 chars), questions: Question[]|null}
types.Question: {question: string, header: string|null, multi_select: boolean, options: {label: string, description: string|null}[]}

ipc_contract.serde: Rust structs use rename_all snake_case so the field names above are the wire names exactly; Answer uses tag = kind, rename_all snake_case, deny_unknown_fields.

s1.$comment: RE-REVIEWS NEST, and this is the rule every reader follows. The TOP LEVEL of reviews.<slice> IS attempt 1. A re-review writes attempt_2, then attempt_3, and so on, each with the same fields as the top level. Every attempt SURVIVES PERMANENTLY - history is never overwritten, flattened, or migrated up. The LATEST attempt supplies the verdict: that is what close-run.py, brief.py and verify-state.py resolve through, and what fleetview's finalVerdict() has always shown. `ever_rejected` - did ANY attempt REJECT - is DISPLAY ONLY, forever, so a rejection stays visible after it is fixed; it must never gate anything, or the fleet stops being able to loop. NO NODE MAY REWRITE AN EARLIER ATTEMPT: a second reviewer writes its own attempt_N and leaves the ones before it alone, top-level verdict included - relocating that verdict would destroy the history the board keeps and leave a key stamped written_by:reviewer with someone else as its real author. The KEY INDEX numbers an attempt, not the `attempt` field inside it; the field is display. An EMPTY attempt_N is not a re-review, it is a key nobody wrote - write the whole attempt or none of it. The walk STOPS AT THE FIRST GAP, so an attempt_3 with no attempt_2 is ignored and the earlier verdict stands: A GAP IS MALFORMED AND NO NODE MAY LEAVE ONE. Write the next UNUSED N and never skip - a mis-numbered re-review is not reported anywhere, it is simply unread, and a REJECT nobody reads is a REJECT nobody acts on. The cap is attempt_9, matching fleetview's `for (i = 2; i < 10; i++)` exactly so the two readers cannot disagree; attempt_10 and beyond is reported loudly and resolved by nobody.

findings.detail: Finished.onClick calls setText('') right after send() without awaiting it, so if answer() rejects (e.g. session ended), the typed reply is lost while the error banner shows. Await send and clear only on success.

Intent says finished -> 'last_message plus a reply box', but InboxItem in ipc_contract has no last_message field; builder renders item.summary. This is the right reading of the contract. Backend slice should make summary carry the final message for finished items.

Subscribes first, then loads. If a session-updated event lands while list_sessions is in flight, the later sessions-loaded can overwrite it with an older snapshot. Narrow window, and the next event corrects it. Questions answers are also keyed by question text, so two questions with identical text would share state. That is acceptable given the Record<string,string> contract.

Seam for integration: invoke passes {args:{...}} for start_session/answer/stop_session, so the Rust command parameters must be named `args` (as the contract writes them). s1 has no commands yet, so this could not be checked against Rust.

Six notes, no blockers.

findings.detail: kill() calls TerminateProcess on claude.exe only. Grandchildren it spawned (Bash tool commands, MCP servers) can outlive stop_session and app exit. A Windows Job Object with KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE would make 'children killed' true for the whole tree.

start_session and answer are sync commands, so they run on the Tauri main thread and do a blocking pipe write: a prompt up to 32 KB, or an allow response echoing a large Write input. If claude is slow to drain stdin, the UI freezes until it does. This is not a deadlock, because the reader thread and emit don't need the main thread. Making these async would move the write off the main thread.

start() fires the summary it captured before spawning (status starting) after send_line returns. If the reader thread has already emitted a newer status, s3's reducer replaces it with the stale starting. The window is narrow and the next stream event corrects it. The invoke return value has the same staleness.

send_through mutates state (item resolved, status working) before send_line. If the write fails, the item stays resolved with nothing delivered and no event fired. The child is killed and the following Exit marks the session failed, so the session recovers visibly. The state.rs comment 'State changes only on success' holds only within the state layer.

A control_request with any subtype other than can_use_tool is counted as Unknown and never answered. That matches s1 (no other subtype was observed), but if a future claude sends one that expects a reply, the session would stall in working with no inbox item.
If stdout closes while the child stays alive, the reader thread polls try_wait every 50 ms until stop or app exit. The builder disclosed this; it is a cheap leak, not a hang.
